Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

prove verb

turn out to be

also turn out, turn out to be, prove true, prove false, prove useless

classical

Cic. Div. 2.108: sī quandō aliquod somnium vērum ēvāserit
Liv. 23.12.12: vāna ēvādat

ēvādō, ēvādere, ēvāsī, ēvāsum

verb, third conjugation, intransitive, with a predicate adjective or noun · Conjugation on Wiktionary

turn out, prove (true, false, empty)

Of how a thing turns out (vērum, vānum), and of what a person becomes: perfectus Epicūrius ēvāserat (Cic. Brut. 131).

Other words

  • exsistō, exsistere, exstitī, exstitum — arise, turn out (to be)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.104.1: ex amīcīs inimīcī exsistunt · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • sī quandō aliquod somnium vērum ēvāserit

    if ever some dream has turned out trueCic. Div. 2.108

  • vereor, nē haec quoque laetitia luxuriet nōbīs ac vāna ēvādat

    I fear that this joy too may run riot with us and prove emptyLiv. 23.12.12

  • ut plērumque in calamitāte ex amīcīs inimīcī exsistunt

    as friends so often turn out enemies in misfortuneCaes. BC 3.104.1

See also prove, appear, seem.
